t: For an additional amount for “Operating Expenses of the Agency for International Development”, $2,000,000, to remain available until expended.

fable.w: This is a bare appropriation of additional operating funds for a federal agency. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: For an additional amount for “Operating Expenses of the Agency for International Development”, $2,000,000, to remain available until expended.

opus.w: This section only gives $2,000,000 more for USAID's operating expenses. It sets up no consultation, hearing, advisory body, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue. No one outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision, so it is not participation.
opus.b: This is a plain appropriation of money. The only thing that might look tempting is the word "Agency," but no outside party takes part in any decision here.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple appropriations provision allocating funds for operating expenses. It does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. There are no mentions of public comments, hearings, advisory boards with non-federal members, or coordination with states or tribes.
qwen_chat.s: For an additional amount for “Operating Expenses of the Agency for International Development”, $2,000,000, to remain available until expended.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "Operating Expenses" could implicitly include costs for public hearings or consultations. However, this is a pure appropriations clause providing funds without specifying any procedural requirements for public involvement. It does not mandate or even suggest any interaction with outside parties.
